title: Tenant-priority reshard and regional fallback orchestration
creator: Marco Chen
description: Customers intermittently observed 5-15s tail latency spikes during cross-region capacity pressure when tenant traffic was being shifted between regions. Impact surfaced across Hosted and Dedicated customers with multi-tenant routing; a subset of high-throughput tenants saw requests held in scheduling queues while KV caches became inconsistent. This ticket tracks the engineering work to implement a deterministic tenant-priority reshard and regional fallback orchestration that minimizes impact during region-level degradations and provides a clear operator runbook for graceful tenant drain, KV reconciliation, and staged failovers.
mitigation_runbook:
1) Detect: Alert triggers when regional p95 latency > 2x SLA and inflight queue depth on region > 80% for 3 consecutive minutes.
2) Triage: SRE confirms region health via cluster-metrics dashboard (Grafana) and per-tenant queue heatmap. Post an incident header in #incidents and tag stakeholders.
3) Soft-throttle: Apply routing throttle policy to non-priority tenants in the impacted region (reduce new session acceptance by 30%). Monitor for immediate queue reduction.
4) Tenant-priority reshuffle: Using tenant priority list (stored in config-service), perform a staged reshard: move low-priority tenants first to warm-standby replicas in secondary region, then medium, leaving high-priority tenants until capacity frees or until fallback threshold reached. Each reshard batch uses a 60s observation window.
5) KV consistency: After each tenant move, trigger KV cache reconciliation for that tenant (invalidate prefix caches and warm using recently observed prefixes). Wait for KV-sync success metric. If reconciliation fails, mark tenant move as failed and queue for manual patch.
6) Fallback escalation: If queue depth does not improve after moving 50% of traffic and latency remains > 1.5x SLA for 10 minutes, promote fallback: route 80% of affected tenant traffic to secondary region with sticky-session draining for remaining 20%.
7) Customer comms: Notify affected tenant owners via the escalation contacts with status updates at 10min cadence. Use templated message in Confluence: CrossRegionFallbackTemplate.
8) Stabilize: Once metrics return under thresholds for 15 minutes, reverse staged moves in reverse order, validate KV consistency and trace sampling for correctness.
9) Post-incident: Capture timeline, decisions and metric graphs. Open follow-up issues for automation gaps.
rollback_plan: If a staged tenant move causes increased errors or cache desyncs: 1) Immediately stop new routing changes. 2) Re-route newly moved tenant traffic back to original region (use sticky cookie/session pinning when possible). 3) Roll back routing config commits (automated feature-flag toggle) and rehydrate KV from latest tombstone snapshots. 4) If rollback fails, escalate to SRE lead and Platform Eng for live DB patch. 5) Document rollback step and mark tenant as blocked until manual verification.
acceptance_criteria: Automated staged reshard API implemented and tested in canary cluster
Telemetry: per-tenant queue depth and KV-sync success metrics added to runtime dashboard
Runbook run-through completed with SRE and Platform Eng (dry-run) and checklist signed off
End-to-end e2e test that simulates cross-region capacity pressure shows <30% of high-priority tenant requests impacted (latency degradation)
postmortem_tasks: Collect per-tenant trace logs for the incident window
Quantify cost impact of cross-region burst and estimate billing adjustments for affected customers
Automate tenant-priority reshard UI in Console and add RBAC check
Add automated canary test to CI that simulates KV cache desync during rehome
